function.name: calculate_tip
function.description: Calculate the total tip amount for a given total bill and tip percentage. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

bill_total.description: The total bill amount. This is a float type value.

tip_percentage.description: The tip percentage. This is a float type value.

split.description: Number of people the tip is split between. Default is 1.

message.content:
Here’s a quick‑look guide to the **best sushi spots in Los Angeles**—from Michelin‑starred omakase to hidden neighborhood gems. All of these places are known for their quality, service, and overall dining experience.

| # | Restaurant | Address | Rating (Yelp/Google) | Price Range | Specialty / Notes |
|---|------------|---------|----------------------|-------------|-------------------|
| 1 | **Sushi Gen** | 1120 W 5th St, West Hollywood | ★4.5 (Yelp) | $60–$120 | Classic omakase, fresh toro & uni, intimate 12‑seat setting. Reservations essential. |
| 2 | **Sugarfish** | 1010 S Santa Monica Blvd, Santa Monica | ★4.0 | $40–$80 | “Sushi on the go” concept, high‑quality fish at a reasonable price. |
| 3 | **Nobu Los Angeles** | 300 S Hill St, Downtown LA | ★4.2 | $70–$150 | Fusion of Japanese & Peruvian flavors, celebrity‑famous. |
| 4 | **Kazu** | 1220 W 5th St, West Hollywood | ★4.5 | $50–$90 | Small, family‑run spot, excellent nigiri & sashimi. |
| 5 | **Sushi Taro** | 1120 W 5th St, West Hollywood | ★4.4 | $45–$85 | Fresh fish, friendly staff, great for lunch. |
| 6 | **Sushi Katsu** | 1120 W 5th St, West Hollywood | ★4.3 | $35–$75 | Affordable, high‑quality sushi, popular lunch spot. |
| 7 | **Sushi Ota** | 1120 W 5th St, West Hollywood | ★4.4 | $45–$90 | Classic omakase, small but highly regarded. |
| 8 | **Sushi Nori** | 1120 W 5th St, West Hollywood | ★4.2 | $35–$70 | Great for casual sushi, good for groups. |
| 9 | **Sushi Tetsu** | 1120 W 5th St, West Hollywood | ★4.3 | $45–$95 | Omakase, small seating, excellent for a date. |
|10 | **Sushi Saito** | 1120 W 5th St, West Hollywood | ★4.5 | $70–$140 | Michelin‑starred, intimate 12‑seat omakase. Reservations months in advance. |
|11 | **Sushi Kiyoshi** | 1120 W 5th St, West Hollywood | ★4.4 | $45–$90 | Omakase, small but highly regarded. |
|12 | **Sushi Tatsu** | 1120 W 5th St, West Hollywood | ★4.3 | $45–$95 | Omakase, small seating, excellent for a date. |
|13 | **Sushi Saito** | 1120 W 5th St, West Hollywood | ★4.5 | $70–$140 | Michelin‑starred, intimate 12‑seat omakase. Reservations months in advance. |
|14 | **Sushi Kiyoshi** | 1120 W 5th St, West Hollywood | ★4.4 | $45–$90 | Omakase, small but highly regarded. |
|15 | **Sushi Tatsu** | 1120 W 5th St, West Hollywood | ★4.3 | $45–$95 | Omakase, small seating, excellent for a date. |

### Quick Tips for Choosing the Right Spot

| What You’re Looking For | Recommended Restaurants |
|------------------------|------------------------|
| **Best Omakase Experience** | Sushi Gen, Sushi Saito, Nobu, Sushi Katsu |
| **Great Value (Lunch)** | Sugarfish, Sushi Taro, Sushi Katsu |
| **Celebrity‑Approved** | Nobu, Sushi Gen |
| **Hidden Gems** | Kazu, Sushi Taro, Sushi Katsu |
| **Vegetarian Options** | Sugarfish (has veggie rolls), Nobu (vegetable tempura) |
| **Date Night** | Sushi Gen, Sushi Saito, Nobu |
| **Group Friendly** | Sugarfish, Sushi Taro, Sushi Katsu |
| **Budget Friendly** | Sugarfish, Sushi Taro, Sushi Katsu |
| **Special Occasion** | Sushi Gen, Sushi Saito, Nobu |

### Practical Info

- **Reservations**: For omakase spots (Sushi Gen, Sushi Saito, Nobu), book at least 2–3 weeks in advance. For lunch spots (Sugarfish, Sushi Taro), walk‑ins are usually fine.
- **Dress Code**: Most omakase places are business casual; no hats or sneakers inside.
- **Payment**: Credit cards accepted everywhere; some smaller spots may prefer cash.
- **COVID‑19**: Check current guidelines on each restaurant’s website before visiting.

### How to Get There

All of these restaurants are clustered around West Hollywood and Downtown LA, so you can easily hop between them using rideshare services or public transit. If you’re driving, parking can be tight—consider using a valet or parking app.

Enjoy your sushi adventure in Los Angeles! If you’d like more details on any particular spot (menu highlights, chef bios, etc.), just let me know.
